ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system xOy, if the line $y_1=-2x+a$ and the line $y_2=bx-4$ intersect at point $P(1, -3)$, what is the solution set of the inequality $-2x+a<bx-4$ with respect to x?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $x>1$, the graph of the function $y_{1}=-2x+a$ is entirely below the graph of $y_{2}=bx-4$. Hence, the solution set of the inequality $-2x+a<bx-4$ is $x>1$;\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x>1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a Cartesian coordinate system xOy with two labeled straight lines. The line y1 is downward-sloping, the line y2 is upward-sloping, and they intersect at the marked point P. The diagram and question indicate this point is P(1,-3). Reasoning: Because P lies on y1 = -2x + a, substitute x = 1 and y = -3: -3 = -2(1) + a, so a = -1. Because P also lies on y2 = bx - 4, substitute x = 1 and y = -3: -3 = b(1) - 4, so b = 1. The inequality -2x + a < bx - 4 becomes -2x - 1 < x - 4. Adding 2x to both sides gives -1 < 3x - 4. Adding 4 gives 3 < 3x, hence x > 1.
